headline: High risk of capability conflict and cascading errors: shared mutable file workflows in the marketing agent can collide with EMQX’s networked IoT context, while prompt-injection and leakage are lower due to no documented shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented between emqx and marketingskills, so direct prompt injection is not evidenced. However, marketingskills references shared context and file-based skills, and emqx can ingest HTTP API content; if operators bridge them via copy-paste or shared files, instruction hijacking becomes plausible. This is lower severity because the bridge is not default.
conditions: IF operators manually copy marketingskills output into emqx prompts or files, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, prompt content can be treated as instructions.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste handoff for untrusted text.
Add a provenance header to any transferred content.
Review any shared file before emqx consumes it.

B_data_leakage.rationale: emqx touches IoT data and has broad network egress, while marketingskills can read and write files and use allowlisted egress. The profiles do not show a shared workspace or shared OAuth principal, so leakage is not default. If operators place sensitive IoT artifacts into marketingskills files, those contents could be exposed through its outbound calls.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory, marketingskills can read IoT artifacts created for emqx.
IF sensitive IoT data is copied into marketingskills inputs, allowlisted outbound requests may transmit it.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Redact IoT payloads before any transfer.
Restrict marketingskills egress allowlist to required domains.
Audit outbound requests for sensitive fields.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: marketingskills has read/write filesystem and subprocess capabilities, and supports multiple instances; emqx has HTTP API access and broad network egress. The pair does not document locking or isolation, so if they share a workspace or mutable config, concurrent edits can overwrite each other. Uncertainty about the actual shared surface keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF both agents mutate shared config or state without locks, race conditions can corrupt outputs.
mitigations: Assign distinct writable directories.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file.
Make shared config read-only for one agent.
Snapshot state before concurrent runs.

D_cascading_error.rationale: marketingskills is explicitly built around skills that reference each other and build on shared context, so it may treat upstream text as reusable guidance. emqx can emit API-driven content that marketingskills could repackage into marketing outputs. There is no documented verification step between them, so errors can cascade into incorrect downstream work products.
conditions: IF emqx output is fed into marketingskills without review, factual errors can propagate.
IF marketingskills is used to draft customer-facing text from emqx outputs, incorrect claims can be published.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before publication.
Require source links for any factual claim.
Compare generated claims against the original emqx output.
Block automatic reuse of unverified context.

E_compliance.rationale: emqx touches IoT data, while marketingskills handles marketing content and product marketing context. The profiles do not show a residency, certification, or retention mismatch, so compliance risk is limited to potential policy drift if IoT data is copied into marketing workflows. Because only emqx is clearly tied to regulated operational data, it is the primary cited agent.
conditions: IF IoT data is transferred into marketing files, retention and disclosure policies may diverge.
IF marketing outputs include regulated operational details, review requirements may be bypassed.
mitigations: Keep IoT data out of marketing workspaces.
Tag regulated fields before transfer.
Apply a retention check before saving shared artifacts.
Review any customer-facing copy for compliance claims.
